verdict.root_cause: At 04:19:13 UTC a platform-automation environment update rewrote cartservice's Redis backend address to point at redis-cart on port 6380, a port nothing is serving on (the conventional port is 6379). The new value took effect on cartservice restart, and from then on cartservice cannot complete the Redis-backed cart store initialization it performs in its startup path: every process start logs a connect attempt to :6380, times out after ~25-40s, throws an unhandled ApplicationException from Main and exits, producing a tight crash-restart loop with at least six identical cycles between 04:23 and 04:26 and no request served. With cartservice absent, checkoutservice's outbound CartService/GetCart client span fails sub-millisecond at connection establishment — no cartservice server span or Redis span exists beneath it — and PlaceOrder aborts before payment, shipping or email are ever called. That error status propagates up through frontend gRPC PlaceOrder to the frontend HTTP POST, which is what alerted at 04:22 alongside loadgenerator, with checkoutservice following at 04:22:15. The failing mechanism is the configuration value itself: the address names a port on which no Redis listener exists, and that wrongness is what breaks every request.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on cartservice's Redis connection target. (1) The change log records exactly one mutation in the window — an environment update at 04:19:13 setting the Redis address to host:6380 — and no deploy, image change or flag flip (tr_d1cc26cefb81); checkoutservice itself has no change at all (tr_3812dbe219c3), so the rollback candidate is not on the alerting service. (2) cartservice logs show the service healthy at 04:12 and then, by 04:23:20, crash-looping with the failure located in the cart store's connect/initialize path called from the entrypoint, naming redis-cart:6380 as the target every cycle (tr_ef8759fc9086). The change and the crash signature name the same non-standard port, which links them causally rather than by timing alone. (3) Traces independently place the deepest error span at checkoutservice's client call to CartService/GetCart with no cartservice server span or Redis span beneath it — the failure occurs before cartservice records any work — and failing traces are sub-millisecond fast-fails, not slow waits (tr_c2ed8108ce8a). That is the signature of calling a process that is not up, matching the crash loop. The empty cartservice call-counter series (tr_a822df8d0c59) is corroborating rather than confusing: a crash-looping process emits no span metrics, which is why the naive 'cart shows zero errors so cart is healthy' reading — the exact mistake recorded in the cart-bad-image-tag corpus entry — must be rejected here. Frontend and checkoutservice error ratios are real but partial (peaks ~31% and ~0.67, with clean-zero baselines in the same window: tr_01c987ecc565, tr_39c88823fcba), consistent with only cart-touching request paths failing while browse traffic succeeds. checkoutservice logs corroborate the shape without naming the cause: order-start lines continue at steady cadence to 04:24:53 while the payment/email/message-write completions that appeared at 04:12 stop (tr_d62763c38653), i.e. orders begin and die at the cart lookup. I classify this bad_config rather than dependency_latency because the service is not failing by waiting — it exits on an unhandled exception at startup and the caller fast-fails in under a millisecond; the ~25-40s connect delay is a TCP timeout to a dead port, not a slow dependency serving requests. It is not bad_deploy because the artifact is unchanged; only an environment variable moved. It is not resource_exhaustion because nothing ran out. The wrong port value is itself the mechanism, so restoring the prior Redis address (or pointing it at a listener that actually exists) is the fix; restarting cartservice without reverting the value would only restart the loop.
open_questions: Whether the intended target really was 6379 and 6380 is a typo, or whether this was a deliberate Redis migration whose server-side half (a listener on 6380) never landed or landed late — nobody queried the Redis/redis-cart side at all, so we have not confirmed what is or is not listening on either port.

The change record shows no prior value for the variable (tr_d1cc26cefb81), so the exact state to revert to is not established by this evidence and must be read from the deployment manifest or the pipeline that pushed it.

The ~3-minute gap between the 04:19:13 config write and the 04:22:00 frontend alert is unexplained by the dispatches — presumably rollout/restart timing, but no pod or replica event data was gathered, and cartservice logs place the visible crash loop only from 04:23:20.

Why checkoutservice emits no error- or warning-severity logs for a failing downstream call (tr_d62763c38653) — an observability gap that delayed attribution and is worth a follow-up independent of this incident.

The middle of the checkoutservice log window was truncated (tr_d62763c38653), so the exact transition from completing to non-completing orders cannot be dated from logs; the trace and change evidence carry that dating instead.

Triage crossed 4 unmeasured edges across 12 affected services; only frontend, checkoutservice and cartservice were examined. Whether other cart-dependent services (e.g. the storefront cart page) are independently degraded, and whether any service was affected by something other than this cart outage, was not checked.
Whether the same automation pushed this variable to other services or environments — the blast radius of the pipeline change itself was never queried.
